episodes.171214: A couple of thunderstorms produced gusty winds and hail over and near area waterways, particularly Baltimore Inner Harbor and the tidal Patapsco River during the afternoon.
episodes.171229: A cold front moving through the area caused the development of some strong thunderstorms, one of which became severe.
episodes.171248: Deep subtropical moisture lingered over the Four Corners region. This resulted in another round of diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. A localized debris flow occurred in San Miguel County.
episodes.171253: The upper-level high pressure system was located over the Great Basin area on August 16, 2022, while a backdoor front moved into eastern New Mexico before stalling along the east slopes of the central mountain chain. Increased moisture and favorable upslope flow supported increasing thunderstorm coverage across much of northeast New Mexico. With already saturated soils from an active monsoon season, the stage was already set across this area for flash flooding. New Mexico's largest burn scar was hit once again with strong thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall, flooding areas that have been repeatedly hit this summer. Meanwhile, heavy rain also impacts northwest New Mexico near the Arizona border, causing devastating flash flooding around Sheep Springs.
episodes.171254: Thunderstorms that originally developed across the Arrowhead of Minnesota early Wednesday morning, August 17th, created a boundary farther southward across east-central Minnesota. This boundary, with daytime heating leading to more instability, caused additional thunderstorms to develop. Due to weak winds aloft, these storms drifted southward but continued to redevelop on the west side. This led to storms training over the same areas from Mora, southward to the eastern portion of the Twin Cities metro area. One area near Cambridge had over 4 inches of rain in less than 2 hours that led to flash flooding in the town. A local business had water damage due to the excessive rainfall. Other areas in the Twin Cities also had excessive rainfall, but only minor flooding occurred, and mainly in poor drainage areas.
episodes.171256: An easterly wave was located just south of El Paso, Texas on August 17, 2022. Associated with this wave was an above normal amount of moisture that produced persistent shower activity across southern New Mexico. This stratiform precipitation moved into southern Lincoln County during the early morning hours of August 17th. While this activity was not convective in nature and did not have very high rain rates, it did move over the McBride burn scar and several hours of even light, steady rain produced flash flooding on the burn scar near Ruidoso. Meanwhile, more typical convective activity in northwest New Mexico produced flash flooding at Chaco National Park.
episodes.171272: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic, minor wind damage during the afternoon hours between northeastern Maryland and Washington, DC.
episodes.171273: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic, minor wind damage during the afternoon hours between northeastern Maryland and Washington, DC.
episodes.171303: An upper low nearby and afternoon instability resulted in isolated strong thunderstorms that produced a lot of small hail. An isolated thunderstorm produced penny sized hail.
episodes.171691: A weak lake-induced surface trough over Lake Erie was accompanied by a land breeze convergence zone in vicinity of the lake's major axis. Ascent accompanying the low-level convergence zone amidst large lake-induced CAPE led to the development of a broken line of lake-effect showers and thunderstorms. Low-level horizontal wind shear along the land breeze convergence zone generated surface-based vertical vorticity. One of the storm's updrafts ingested this surface-based vertical vorticity, stretched it to tornado-strength via low-level convergence at the updraft's base, and then the tornado-strength vertical vorticity was advected upward in the updraft, resulting in waterspout formation.
episodes.171881: Morning thunderstorms produce waterspouts near Clearwater and Redington beaches and gusty marine winds across coastal waters around west central Florida.
episodes.171921: A thunderstorm became severe in western Volusia County where it produced tree and powerline damage in Orange City.
episodes.171922: Thunderstorms pushing offshore from the Volusia and Brevard County coasts produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.172102: Non-severe storms passed through Steuben County in Central New York during the afternoon hours. An 80 year old man was injured aftering getting struck by lightning from a passing storm.
episodes.172133: A weak trade wind regime and plenty of low-level moisture caused heavy showers to develop over windward locales of Oahu.  The precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.172182: An elongated tropical wave moved across the Caribbean sea, while a weakening surface trough crosses just northeast of the region. The moisture provided by these features generated strong shower activity over the island.
episodes.172230: A front was stalled near the FL-GA state line. SW steering flow pushed a stronger west coast sea breeze front inland through the day, with further enhancement as the sea breezes merged near the St. Johns River basin in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.172233: A front was stalled near the FL-GA state line. SW steering flow pushed a stronger west coast sea breeze front inland through the day, with further enhancement as the sea breezes merged near the St. Johns River basin in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.172247: A thunderstorm became severe over southwestern portions of Butte County, producing strong wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.172250: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northern Butte County, producing some wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.172253: Strong winds from a decaying line of thunderstorms produced wind gusts to 60 mph over portions of eastern Pennington County.
episodes.172446: There was an upper level low pressure system over Northern Mexico. A cold front was across the Permian Basin. These features brought an increase in lift across West Texas. High low-level moisture was in place. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced high wind gusts in Brewster County.
episodes.172712: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 16th, as a cold front moved through the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172784: A few stronger storms developed over Baca County on August 16th and produced very heavy rainfall.
episodes.173204: A summer cold front helped to ignite thunderstorms primarily along and south of the Interstate 20 corridor on the evening of Wednesday August 17. Damaging wind gusts associated with microbursts accompanied a few of these storms.
episodes.173222: An atmospheric river front brought periods of heavy rain to the northern panhandle starting Tuesday evening August 16th, particularly at elevation. There was also significant warm temperature over the area that increased the amount of ice melt from glaciers in the Taiya River basin. A frontal wave along enhanced rainfall rates again Wednesday morning August 17th. Rainfall amounts in the headwaters of the Taiya River ranged from 1.50 to 2 inches for the event. The Taiya River went over moderate flood stage and flooded the lower portions of the Chilkoot trail with cold and swift water up to knee deep in places.
episodes.173315: Despite high pressure in place across much of the region on the 17th, a few slow moving storms developed across northeastern Minnesota during the afternoon hours. Heavy rainfall was the primary concern with these storms due to their slow movement, but no reports of flash flooding were received. One storm was able to produce hail to the size of golf balls as it moved across Aitkin and Carlton counties, but otherwise the storms remained below severe limits.
episodes.173326: Upper ridging over the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles that extended east into the Mississippi Valley through much of the summer, finally retreated back west on August 17th, ahead of a weak upper trough that dug southeast into the Four State Region. This trough reinforced a stationary front south into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon, with these features providing the necessary forcing for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms. Available moisture and very strong heating during the afternoon contributed to very unstable conditions across these areas as temperatures climbed into the lower 100s, resulting in isolated severe thunderstorms developing over Grant Parish in Central Louisiana. These storms produced damaging winds which downed trees throughout the parish before weakening during the evening.
episodes.173327: Upper ridging over the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles that extended east into the Mississippi Valley through much of the summer, finally retreated back west on August 17th, ahead of a weak upper trough that dug southeast into the Four State Region. This trough reinforced a stationary front south into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon, with these features providing the necessary forcing for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms. Available moisture and very strong heating during the afternoon contributed to very unstable conditions across these areas as temperatures climbed into the lower 100s, resulting in isolated severe thunderstorms developing over Wood County in East Texas. These storms produced damaging winds which downed trees as well as large hail throughout the county before weakening during the evening.
episodes.173380: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on August 17, 2022 in association with a disturbance off the Northeast US coast. These storms tracked from northeast to southwest. Damage was mainly confined to the Capital Region where a severe thunderstorm downed some trees and power lines across the region. In addition, sub-severe wind gusts led to some flying debris at the New York State Food Festival which was being held in Albany. Event managers cancelled the remainder of the event following the storm.
episodes.173469: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines along with heavy rain which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.173541: Abundant moisture (1.8-2.0) and an unstable environment (MUCAPE 2,000-4,000 J/kg) across south-central and southwest Arizona allowed for convective development to become strong to severe. Thunderstorms initiated over the high terrain of northern Arizona before working toward the south into the lower deserts. Severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts upwards of 60-70 mph along with several reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
episodes.173611: An upper low nearby and afternoon instability resulted in isolated strong thunderstorms that produced a lot of small hail. This was another day of thunderstorms moving generally from east to west and rather slowly. An isolated thunderstorm near Darien Center produced nickel sized hail.
episodes.173647: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced damaging winds in Oro Valley.
episodes.173734: A trough over the eastern United States produced a southwest to west wind flow across South Florida, leading to scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours across SE Florida.
episodes.173800: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173801: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173929: Despite a lack radar returns, enhanced development within a cumulus field resulted in a funnel cloud spotted in western Iowa. While no precipitation or damage occurred, the environment was favorable for funnel cloud development owing to low-level 0-3 km CAPE just over 100 J/kg.
episodes.173974: Deep monsoon moisture remained over northern Arizona with heavy rain producing thunderstorms.
episodes.173983: A cold front approached the region from the northeast on August 16th. As is common during the summertime, the cold front stalled before reaching the local area. This boundary began to slowly sag southward on the 17th. As storms developed in the vicinity of the stalled front, they began to intensity somewhat quickly. This was due to the fact that it was already in the afternoon hours and intense daytime heating substantially increased instability ahead of these southward moving storms. One storm strengthened enough to reach severe limits and produced damaging winds in Jackson County.
episodes.173984: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona brought thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.174063: Very heavy rainfall occurred over Webb and Duval Counties associated with a tropical low pressure system on the 15th and 16th. Flood wave that originated in San Casamiro Creek in Webb County flowed into the Nueces River, Major river flooding occurred from southeast La Salle County through McMullen County to Live Oak County from the 17th through the 24th.

The atmospheric river produced 1 to 2 inches fell over 24hrs with highest rainfall amounts at higher elevations. In addition to the rainfall there was significant snow and ice melt from very warm temps in the headwaters of the Taiya River basin and the main tributary of the Norse River basin. Rain moved into the area the night of 16th and increased through the early morning hours of the 17th and persisted into the afternoon before the rainfall moved east of the area by the late afternoon on the 17th.||The Taiya River started to rise from the moderate to heavy rain in the evening of August 16th and went over minor flood stage of 16.5 feet mid morning of August 17th and crested at 17.58 feet around 330pm which is above moderate flood stage of 17.0 feet. The river did not drop below minor flood stage until the early morning hours of August 18th. The Klondike NHP closed the Chilkoot trail to all use on August 17th. The flooding had submerged sections of the Chilkoot Trail with hazardous, swift-flowing, waist-deep water.
